title: Fixed/floating-strike lookback calls and puts: closed form vs GBM Monte Carlo
frame: DIKETAHUI: daily closes; r, D given (b = r - D); grid T [3] x moneyness [5], K = S0 m; N_paths, steps/year, seed as stated. DITANYAKAN: calibration.json; fixed_strike_lookback.csv (T,K,moneyness,cf_price,mc_price,mc_std_err) 15 rows; floating_strike_lookback.csv (T,type,cf_price,mc_price,mc_std_err) 6 rows; summary.json. RUMUS: x = ln(P_t/P_{t-1}); sigma = std(x, ddof=1) sqrt(252); GSG floating call/put and Conze-Viswanathan fixed call with M = m = S0; MC price = e^{-rT} mean(payoff), se = e^{-rT} std(payoff)/sqrt(N); mc_validates = all(|cf - mc| < 2 se). DECISIVE: build every CSV row as ONE dict inside the loop that produced its numbers: for typ in (call, put): for T in Ts: rows.append({T, type, cf_price, mc_price, mc_std_err}); never pair np.repeat(Ts, 2) / np.tile(types) with np.concatenate([calls, puts]) - the labels then sit on the wrong prices and 'prices increase with T' fails. JAWAB: 1) calibration. 2) closed forms. 3) MC per T, running max/min including the t=0 column. 4) rows as dicts -> DataFrame. 5) assert per type that cf_price increases with T, per T that fixed prices fall with K. 6) summary from the same rows.
formulas: sigma = std(log returns, ddof=1) * sqrt(252); S0 = last close; n_returns = len(close) - 1

float call (GSG, m=S0): S e^{-DT} N(a1) - m e^{-rT} N(a2) + S e^{-rT} (sigma^2/(2b)) [ (S/m)^{-2b/sigma^2} N(-a1 + 2b sqrt(T)/sigma) - e^{bT} N(-a1) ], a1 = [ln(S/m) + (b + sigma^2/2)T]/(sigma sqrt T), a2 = a1 - sigma sqrt T
float put (GSG, M=S0): M e^{-rT} N(-b2) - S e^{-DT} N(-b1) + S e^{-rT} (sigma^2/(2b)) [ e^{bT} N(b1) - (S/M)^{-2b/sigma^2} N(b1 - 2b sqrt(T)/sigma) ]
fixed call (Conze-Viswanathan), K > M=S0: BS call + S e^{-rT} (sigma^2/(2b)) [ e^{bT} N(d1) - (S/K)^{-2b/sigma^2} N(d1 - 2b sqrt(T)/sigma) ]; K <= M: e^{-rT}(M-K) + same with K -> M
MC: mc_price = e^{-rT} mean(payoff); mc_std_err = e^{-rT} std(payoff, ddof=1)/sqrt(N_paths); dt = 1/252, n_steps = round(T*252)
max_mc_error_fixed = max |cf_price - mc_price| over the 15 rows; mc_validates = all(|cf - mc| < 2 * mc_std_err)
steps: Floating table: rows = []; for typ in ['call', 'put']: for i, T in enumerate(Ts): rows.append({'T': T, 'type': typ, 'cf_price': cf[typ][i], 'mc_price': mc[typ][i], 'mc_std_err': se[typ][i]}); df = pd.DataFrame(rows). Fixed table likewise: for T: for m: rows.append({...}).

Load the daily CSV, sort by date, take the Close column; compute log returns; n_returns, return_mean, return_std (ddof=1), sigma = return_std*sqrt(252), S0 = last close -> calibration.json with r and D as given.
Build the grids: T list [3], moneyness list [5], K = S0*m [15 rows]; the floating grid is T only [3 calls + 3 puts].
Closed forms (toolkit lookback_fixed_price, lookback_floating_price or card Core 3) per row; keep them as float arrays aligned to the rows.

Monte Carlo: np.random.seed(seed) once; for each T draw Z [N_paths x n_steps], log path = cumsum((r - sigma^2/2)dt + sigma sqrt(dt) Z) prefixed with 0, S = S0 exp(.); M_T = max over axis 1, m_T = min over axis 1, S_T = last column; never loop over paths.
Fixed-strike payoffs for all 5 strikes at once: np.maximum(M_T[:, None] - K_row[None, :], 0) -> shape [N x 5]; floating call S_T - m_T, floating put M_T - S_T [N].

mc_price and mc_std_err per row (discount both); assemble fixed_strike_lookback.csv with columns T,K,moneyness,cf_price,mc_price,mc_std_err and floating_strike_lookback.csv with T,type,cf_price,mc_price,mc_std_err (type in {call, put}).

summary.json: sigma, S0, n_fixed_strike = len(fixed rows), n_floating_strike = len(floating rows), max errors, mc_validates (bool), atm_fixed_T025/T050/T100 = fixed cf_price at m=1 for each T, float_call_T050 and float_put_T050 at T=0.5; cast every value with float()/int()/bool().
conventions: Floating CSV rows: list of dicts from a nested loop (type outer: call then put; T inner ascending) so each 'type' label sits on its own price; never np.repeat/np.tile labels against an np.concatenate of values.
Self-check before writing: within each type cf_price and mc_price strictly increase with T; within each T fixed-strike prices decrease with K. A failure means misaligned rows, not a pricing error.

Keys exactly as listed: sigma, S0, n_fixed_strike, n_floating_strike, max_mc_error_fixed, max_mc_error_floating, mc_validates, atm_fixed_T025, atm_fixed_T050, atm_fixed_T100, float_call_T050, float_put_T050; calibration.json carries sigma and S0 too.
Floating CSV type column uses lowercase 'call' and 'put'; rows ordered calls (T ascending) then puts (T ascending).
sigma is the annualised decimal vol; prices in currency; floats as Python float, counts as int, flags as bool.
D=0 means b=r; use the b -> 2b/sigma^2 exponent form (never divide by zero if b=0: use a tiny b).
pitfalls: Floating CSV assembled with np.repeat(T, 2) + np.tile(['call','put']) next to np.concatenate([call_prices, put_prices]): row labels and values misalign (call at T=1 lands on a 'put' row) and the monotone-in-T tests fail.
Shape mismatch when broadcasting K [5] against path extremes [N]: use M_T[:, None] - K[None, :] (or loop over the 5 strikes), never a flat 15-grid against the path array.
Omitting sigma from summary.json or any of the atm_fixed_Txxx / float_*_T050 keys fails required-field tests.
Running extremes must include the t=0 column (S0) so floating payoffs are nonnegative.
np.float64 scalars into json: cast with float().

title: Discrete arithmetic Asian calls: exact geometric, Levy, Curran, and MC benchmark
frame: DIKETAHUI: closes -> S0, sigma = std(log ret) sqrt(252); r given; grid T [2] x n_monitoring [3] x moneyness [3] = 18 rows, K = S0 m; N_mc paths; dates t_i = i T/n, i = 1..n (exclude t=0). DITANYAKAN: asian_prices.csv (T,n_monitoring,K,moneyness,geo_exact,levy_arith,curran_arith,mc_arith,mc_geo,mc_std_err) sorted by T, n_monitoring, K; summary. RUMUS: geometric exact: Mu = (r - sigma^2/2) T (n+1)/(2n), H = sigma^2 T (n+1)(2n+1)/(6 n^2), F_G = S0 e^{Mu + H/2}, geo = e^{-rT}[F_G N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(F_G/K) + H/2]/sqrt H, d2 = d1 - sqrt H. Levy: M1 = (S0/n) sum e^{r t_i}, M2 = (S0^2/n^2) sum_ij e^{r(t_i+t_j) + sigma^2 min(t_i,t_j)}, v^2 = ln(M2/M1^2), levy = e^{-rT}[M1 N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(M1/K) + v^2/2]/v. Curran: card exotic-options Core 4 (mu_i, s_i^2, s_x, s_xi, K^). MC: paths [N x n] by cumsum of log increments, S_bar = mean, G = exp(mean ln S); mc_arith = e^{-rT} mean max(S_bar-K,0), mc_geo = e^{-rT} mean max(G-K,0), mc_std_err = e^{-rT} std(arith payoff, ddof=1)/sqrt N. JAWAB: 1) calibrate. 2) per (T, n): dates, moment sums via a min(t_i,t_j) matrix, one path set reused for the 3 strikes. 3) rows. 4) summary. 5) write.
formulas: sigma = std(x, ddof=1) sqrt(252), x_i = ln(close_i/close_{i-1}); S0 = last close; n_prices = number of closes
geo_exact: Mu = (r - sigma^2/2) T (n+1)/(2n); H = sigma^2 T (n+1)(2n+1)/(6 n^2); price = e^{-rT}[S0 e^{Mu + H/2} N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(S0/K) + Mu + H]/sqrt(H), d2 = d1 - sqrt(H)

levy_arith: M1 = (S0/n) sum_i e^{r t_i}; M2 = (S0^2/n^2) sum_{i,j} e^{r(t_i + t_j) + sigma^2 min(t_i, t_j)}; v^2 = ln(M2/M1^2); price = e^{-rT}[M1 N(d1) - K N(d2)], d1 = [ln(M1/K) + v^2/2]/v, d2 = d1 - v

curran_arith: mu_i = ln S0 + (r - sigma^2/2) t_i, s_i^2 = sigma^2 t_i, mu = mean(mu_i), s_x^2 = (sigma^2/n^2) sum_ij min(t_i,t_j), s_xi = (sigma^2/n) sum_j min(t_i,t_j); K^ = 2K - (1/n) sum_i exp(mu_i + s_xi (ln K - mu)/s_x^2 + (s_i^2 - s_xi^2/s_x^2)/2); price = e^{-rT}[(1/n) sum_i e^{mu_i + s_i^2/2} N((mu - ln K^)/s_x + s_xi/s_x) - K N((mu - ln K^)/s_x)]

MC: S on dates [N x n]; S_bar = mean axis 1; G = exp(mean(ln S) axis 1); mc_arith = e^{-rT} mean(max(S_bar - K, 0)); mc_geo = e^{-rT} mean(max(G - K, 0)); mc_std_err = e^{-rT} std(max(S_bar-K,0), ddof=1)/sqrt(N)
geo_less_than_arith_pct = 100 * mean(geo_exact < mc_arith); levy_vs_mc_max_error = max|levy_arith - mc_arith|; curran_better_than_levy = curran_vs_mc_max_error < levy_vs_mc_max_error
steps: Load closes (lowercase column names), log returns, return_mean, return_std (ddof=1), sigma, S0, n_prices -> calibration.json.
Grid loops over T then n_monitoring then K ascending (18 rows); dates t = T*arange(1, n+1)/n.
geo_exact via toolkit asian_geometric_price or the closed form; levy via asian_arithmetic_levy; curran via asian_curran (or card formulas) - all vectorisable over K.

MC per (T, n): seed once at the start; Z [N x n]; log increments (r - sigma^2/2) dt_i + sigma sqrt(dt_i) Z with dt_i = T/n; cumsum -> S; compute S_bar and G once and reuse for the 3 strikes; mc_geo must be the discounted mean of max(G - K, 0) (never left at zero).
Assemble asian_prices.csv with exactly the 10 columns in the stated order; sort by T, n_monitoring, K.
summary.json: n_rows = len(table), geo_less_than_arith_pct, levy_vs_mc_max_error, curran_vs_mc_max_error, curran_better_than_levy (bool).
conventions: Monitoring dates exclude t=0 and include T; moneyness = K/S0; prices in currency.
Sort rows by T, n_monitoring, K ascending; keep the column order T,n_monitoring,K,moneyness,geo_exact,levy_arith,curran_arith,mc_arith,mc_geo,mc_std_err.
mc_std_err is the SE of the arithmetic MC price (ddof=1, discounted).
All prices must be strictly positive: compute mc_geo from the geometric average G of the same paths.
pitfalls: mc_geo = 0.0 when the geometric payoff is never computed or G uses a product that underflows: use exp(mean(log S)).
Levy M2 needs the full double sum with min(t_i,t_j); a single sum gives a wrong v^2.
Python float / int / bool casts before json.dump.

title: Merton jump-diffusion MLE calibration, series pricing, BS comparison and implied-vol smile
frame: DECISIVE: rep = merton_jump_diffusion_report(df, dt=, n_max=, bounds=[4 stated (lo, hi)], n_starts=, seed=, r=, maturities=, moneyness=, smile_threshold=); for name, obj in rep.items(): emit(name, obj). analytical_price = down-and-out call (K > B): A - C, A = S N(x1) - K e^{-rT} N(x1 - v), C = S (B/S)^{2(mu+1)} N(y1) - K e^{-rT} (B/S)^{2mu} N(y1 - v), mu = (r - sigma^2/2)/sigma^2, v = sigma sqrt T, x1 = ln(S/K)/v + (1 + mu) v, y1 = ln(B^2/(S K))/v + (1 + mu) v; for K < B use B - D form (toolkit barrier_price)
